verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 7.16
2. Anusayavagga
Aniccānupassīsutta
“Sattime, bhikkhave, puggalā āhuneyyā pāhuneyyā dakkhiṇeyyā añjalikaraṇīyā anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
verses.english: “Mendicants, these seven individuals are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and are the supreme field of merit for the world.

verses.pali: Katame satta?
Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco puggalo sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī viharati, aniccasaññī, aniccapaṭisaṁvedī satataṁ samitaṁ abbokiṇṇaṁ cetasā adhimuccamāno paññāya pariyogāhamāno.
verses.english: First, take an individual who meditates observing impermanence in all conditions. They perceive impermanence and experience impermanence. Constantly, continually, and without interruption, they apply the mind and fathom with wisdom.

verses.pali: So āsavānaṁ khayā …pe… sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati.
verses.english: They’ve realized the undefiled freedom of heart and freedom by wisdom in this very life, and live having realized it with their own insight due to the ending of defilements.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo puggalo āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī viharati, aniccasaññī, aniccapaṭisaṁvedī satataṁ samitaṁ abbokiṇṇaṁ cetasā adhimuccamāno paññāya pariyogāhamāno.
verses.english: Next, take an individual who meditates observing impermanence in all conditions.

verses.pali: Tassa apubbaṁ acarimaṁ āsavapariyādānañca hoti jīvitapariyādānañca.
verses.english: Their defilements and their life come to an end at exactly the same time.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, dutiyo puggalo āhuneyyo …pe… anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
Puna caparaṁ, bhikkhave, idhekacco puggalo sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassī viharati, aniccasaññī, aniccapaṭisaṁvedī satataṁ samitaṁ abbokiṇṇaṁ cetasā adhimuccamāno paññāya pariyogāhamāno.
verses.english: Next, take an individual who meditates observing impermanence in all conditions.

verses.pali: So pañcannaṁ orambhāgiyānaṁ saṁyojanānaṁ parikkhayā antarāparinibbāyī hoti …pe…
verses.english: With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished between one life and the next. …

verses.pali: upahaccaparinibbāyī hoti …pe…
verses.english: With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished upon landing. …

verses.pali: asaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti …pe…
verses.english: With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished without extra effort. …

verses.pali: sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyī hoti …pe…
verses.english: With the ending of the five lower fetters they’re extinguished with extra effort. …

verses.pali: uddhaṁsoto hoti akaniṭṭhagāmī.
verses.english: With the ending of the five lower fetters they head upstream, going to the Akaniṭṭha realm.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, bhikkhave, sattamo puggalo āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassa.
Ime kho, bhikkhave, satta puggalā āhuneyyā pāhuneyyā dakkhiṇeyyā añjalikaraṇīyā anuttaraṁ puññakkhettaṁ lokassā”ti.
verses.english: These are the seven individuals who are worthy of offerings dedicated to the gods, worthy of hospitality, worthy of a religious donation, worthy of greeting with cupped palms, and are the supreme field of merit for the world.”

verses.pali: Chaṭṭhaṁ.
